approach: Add `crates/athena-core/src/gate_counts.rs`, a pure function over `store::Records`. A gate is a failed check name in the verification of a `rejected` job, or `verifier` when none failed, or an admission violation rule on a rejected or failed job. A gate "ended" a job once. It was "overruled" when a later request job, whose text is "try again on <job>" (found with `reading::retried_job`), landed the same change. "Same change": if both candidates carry equal `base_fingerprint`s, the candidate `fingerprint`s must be equal; otherwise the sorted, non-empty `changes` lists (path, status, mode, bytes) must be equal. The counts go to three places. (1) The introspection prompt gets a `gate_counts` array; the schema enum gains `relax` and `remove`; the system prompt says a rule or check can be wrong. (2) `PreventionKind` gains `Relax` and `Remove` (kebab-case, old kinds byte-identical). For these the answer carries a nullable `gate` field. `apply_answer` accepts it only when that gate has ends >= 1 AND disagreements >= 1 (round-3 finding 4); the code stores a `[gate: NAME] ` prefix on `prevention`. (3) Hestia's `error_review` queues one normal-priority request per open gate (a fixed `Gate under review: NAME.` line is the marker, so a second relax for the same gate while that request is open queues nothing; round-3 finding 3). `cause_key` returns None for Relax and Remove, so they join no repeated-cause group, which also keeps them out of `improvement_of`, `plan_backfill` and the status open causes. A relax or remove introspection is a proposal about a check, not a failure case or a retry seed, so code keeps it away from default proposals (round-3 finding 1: `read_records` does not turn it into a `CaseRow`) and away from retries (finding 2: `retry_introspection` skips it). `athena status` gains a `gate_counts` field and a section, most overruled first. Nothing is relaxed or removed, and no config or workflow file is touched.

decisions.choice: Count from existing job records only (request, candidate, verification, outcome). 'Unchanged' is base-independent: equal Some base_fingerprints require equal candidate fingerprints; otherwise sorted non-empty `changes` lists must be equal. At most one end and one disagreement per gate per ended job, so disagreements <= ends.
decisions.reason: The candidate fingerprint hashes the whole governed tree (attrs.rs:135-160, candidate.rs:170-171), so any job landing between a rejected try and its retry changes it. `ChangeEntry` (records.rs:718-723) and `Candidate.base_fingerprint` (records.rs:779) already hold what the base-independent comparison needs. The retry link is `reading::retried_job`. A 'rejected' outcome is exactly a failed verification verdict (run/verification.rs:434-437), so failed check names identify the gate.

rejected.why: Differs almost always once other jobs land between tries, so disagreements stay 0 in a busy repository.
ChangeEntry has byte counts but no content hash; the exact fingerprint is used when the base is equal.

rejected.option: A new record kind or counter file
rejected.why: The brief rules out backfill and new sources; the records hold every fact needed.

rejected.option: Also count a later green rerun or verifier pass as disagreement
rejected.why: A second, fuzzier signal needing more fixtures; criterion 1 asks only for the unchanged-landing signal. Recorded as a user question.

decisions.choice: Name the gate through a nullable answer field `gate` (`#[serde(default)]` in `Answer`); `apply_answer` stores `[gate: NAME] <prevention>` in the existing `prevention` field. `gate_of_prevention` anchors at the start, needs the closing `] `, and Hestia calls it only for Relax and Remove. The docs call the prefix a stopgap until a typed field exists.
decisions.reason: `IntrospectionRecord` has `deny_unknown_fields`; a typed field would need edits at about 13 struct-literal sites outside the deliverables (refusal_corpus.rs:703, proposals.rs:742, evidence_labels.rs:521, labeled.rs:958, briefs.rs:3015, status.rs:2489/3462, hestia.rs:2856, introspect.rs:1355/1823, CLI tests) and would change the record shape the brief puts out of scope.

rejected.why: Out of scope ('changing existing introspection records') and forces edits in many unlisted files.

rejected.option: Find gate names inside the free `prevention` text
rejected.why: Names like `test` occur in any sentence.

decisions.choice: Round-3 finding 4: `apply_answer` accepts relax or remove only for a gate whose counts show disagreements >= 1. Otherwise the record is Failed with 'the model chose {kind} for gate {g}, which no later try overruled', and nothing is queued. The system prompt says the same. `Athena::gate_review` re-reads the counts at queue time and queues nothing for a gate with disagreements 0.
decisions.reason: A loosening proposal with 'overruled 0' as its evidence is thin. The criterion's evidence is the overruled count, so zero cannot support a relax. Code enforces it so a model that ignores the prompt still cannot queue one. Two checks (answer time and queue time) cover a record written by another path.

rejected.why: Case (b) fmt with 5 ends and 0 disagreements would be accepted and queued citing 'overruled 0'.

rejected.option: Record the answer as Recorded and only skip the queue
rejected.why: A Recorded relax with no evidence reads as a finding; failing it matches how every other unsupported answer is handled.

decisions.choice: Hestia queues the gate request for a single relax or remove introspection, with a branch in `error_review` before `try_error_review`. `cause_key` returns None for Relax and Remove.
decisions.reason: Criterion 2 needs one accepted answer to queue a request; the counts are the evidence. `addressing_request` (hestia.rs:282-324) treats a group as addressed when any request text contains any id in the group, so a gate-review request for a relax introspection would hide a code-check of the same cause from the backfill. `cause_key` (hestia.rs:264-274) feeds `repeated_causes`, whose readers are `improvement_of` (hestia.rs:419), `plan_backfill` (hestia.rs:1250), `try_error_review` (hestia.rs:2375) and status open causes (status.rs:2227). With None, a relax introspection is in none of those, and a gate review does not claim to fix a root cause.

rejected.why: Needs two or more distinct jobs with one cause, and its text asks for a root-cause fix.

rejected.option: Keep relax and remove in cause groups
rejected.why: The gate request would suppress root-cause requests for the group's other introspections, and would appear as an improvement item and open cause.

decisions.choice: Round-3 finding 3: dedupe the gate request per gate, not only per introspection id. The request body holds a fixed line `Gate under review: NAME.`. `gate_review` returns None when (a) `addressing_request` finds a request citing this introspection id, or (b) an open (not Closed) request job has a line equal to that marker (helper `open_gate_request`, same shape as `open_request_with_marker` at hestia.rs:1651 but with an exact-line match, so gate `test` does not match `test-all` or `test.x`). A closed (landed, rejected, failed, dropped) gate request does not suppress a new one if new evidence arrives.
decisions.reason: Each rejected job gets its own introspection, so an id-only check would queue one loosening request per rejection when a model keeps answering 'relax test'. A marker on an open request limits it to one review in flight per gate. The id check stays for the one-request-per-introspection case after a request closes.

rejected.why: It matches by `starts_with`, so a marker for `test` also matches `test-all`.

rejected.option: Suppress while any gate request, open or closed, exists
rejected.why: A gate whose review landed with no change would never be reviewed again even with new counts; a person can close a request, and the id check already stops repeats of the same introspection.

decisions.choice: Round-3 finding 1: relax and remove introspections are not cases. `PreventionKind::loosens()` (true for Relax and Remove) is added in records.rs. In `introspect::read_records` (introspect.rs:388-413), a Recorded introspection with a loosening kind is not pushed to `records.cases` and adds nothing to `case_interventions`. A test shows `proposals::generate` makes no proposal from a class whose only cases are relax/remove introspections.
decisions.reason: `generate` (proposals.rs:265-282) groups `records.cases` by failure class and never reads the kind; so three 'this check is wrong' introspections in one class would become a proposal to add a default, the opposite direction. The filter sits where the rows are built so every reader of `cases` (generate at 274, validate at proposals.rs:187, case_interventions at 350, `narrow_cases` at introspect.rs:841, the earlier-case check at introspect.rs:1506) sees the same set. This makes the docs rule at defaults-loop.md lines 381-382 true in code. Consequence, stated in the docs: a relax record cannot be cited as an earlier case.

rejected.why: The doc would state a false rule and the dependent's test could not fail.
Adds a field and edits every CaseRow literal; the one filter at row creation reaches all readers.

decisions.choice: Round-3 finding 2: `reading::retry_introspection` (reading.rs:1413-1428) skips an introspection whose kind is loosening; `retry_cause` also skips earlier cases with a loosening kind (defensive). So a relax record never reaches the retry seed text ('kind: prevention'), `has_retry_introspection` (reading.rs:1516, used at reading.rs:1133) is false for a job whose only introspection is relax, and an older code-check introspection of the same job is still used. Callers of `retry_introspection`: reading.rs:1133 (via has_retry_introspection), reading.rs:1441 (retry_cause), evidence_labels.rs:161 (`retry_vote`).
decisions.reason: A seed saying 'relax: [gate: test] ...' invites the producer of an ordinary 'try again on <job>' to weaken the check; relaxing is out of scope and goes to the Hestia review request instead. Excluding at the source keeps all three callers consistent (evidence_labels then does not count the relax record as the retry's seed, which is correct: it seeded nothing).

rejected.option: Render it in the seed as 'proposal under review, do not act'
rejected.why: Still puts loosening text in front of the producer; adds prompt text with no benefit.
`has_retry_introspection` and `retry_vote` would still treat the relax record as the seed.

risks.risk: On a moved base the change-list comparison (path, status, mode, bytes) has no content hash, so two different edits of equal size to the same files count as 'unchanged' (false disagreement).
risks.mitigation: The exact fingerprint is used whenever both base fingerprints are equal. The change list is used only when the base moved or a base fingerprint is missing, and must be non-empty. The doc and status label state the rule. Tests (c), (d), (e) cover it.

risks.risk: A retry that landed after other jobs changed the same files could match on a change list by coincidence of path and size.
risks.mitigation: Both tries are linked by the explicit 'try again on <job>' text and the retry must be Landed; at most one disagreement per gate per ended job.

risks.risk: Record fixtures for the CLI tests fail `check_record_file` validation or land in `invalid_records`, so counts come out empty.
risks.mitigation: Build them with the same canonical_path/to_json route as review.rs and assert `invalid_records` is empty in the status test. The unit fixture uses the same builders.

risks.risk: A model-chosen gate may contain ']' or a newline and break the prefix parse or the `Gate under review: NAME.` marker line.
risks.mitigation: `gate_counts` omits names containing ']' or newlines, `apply_answer` accepts only names from that list, `gate_of_prevention` is anchored and used only for Relax and Remove, and the marker is matched as a whole line.

risks.risk: Adding a required `gate` property to the strict output schema could make a real model reject or omit it.
risks.mitigation: The property is nullable and `Answer.gate` has `#[serde(default)]`. Other kinds ignore it. The system prompt says to set it null otherwise.

risks.risk: Excluding relax/remove from `cause_key`, `read_records` cases and `retry_introspection` changes behavior in existing repositories.
risks.mitigation: No existing record has these kinds, so no existing group, case or seed changes. Existing hestia, proposals, reading and evidence_labels tests plus the new tests cover it.

risks.risk: Leaving relax records out of `records.cases` means the job's own failure class gets no case from that job, and a relax record cannot be cited as an earlier case.
risks.mitigation: This is the intended effect (a challenge to a check is not evidence for a new default). The docs state it. The failed job's other introspections still count.

risks.risk: Hestia queues loosening requests from thin evidence.
risks.mitigation: The gate must have ends >= 1 and disagreements >= 1 at answer time and again at queue time; at most one open request per gate; the request is a normal-priority review that cites the counts and asks for a justified change. This job relaxes nothing.

risks.risk: A new enum variant or struct field breaks compilation or a lint in a crate the diff does not edit.
risks.mitigation: Step 11 runs the full-workspace fmt, clippy and test commands. `Answer.gate` is `#[serde(default)]` and `IntrospectionRecord` gains no field.

demonstrations.method: Unit tests in gate_counts.rs. A fixture builds AnyRecords (Request, Candidate2, Verification, Outcome) in a tempdir and loads them with `store::Records::load_dir`. Cases: (a) `test` ends 5 rejected jobs, each with a landed 'try again on <job>' retry on the same base_fingerprint and the same candidate fingerprint: ends 5 / disagreements 5. (b) `fmt` ends 5 jobs: 3 retries landed with a different fingerprint on the same base, 2 retries rejected again: disagreements 0. (c) Moved base, different tree fingerprint, identical change list: counts as a disagreement. (d) Moved base, different change list: does not count. (e) Same base, different fingerprint, identical change list: does not count. (f) A rejected job with no failed check counts under `verifier`. (g) A pre-existing-note failed check is not counted. (h) An admission rule is counted. (i) Order is most overruled first.
demonstrations.observes: `gate_counts(&records)` returns `test` with ends 5 and disagreements 5 and `fmt` with ends 5 and disagreements 0; case (c) gives 1, (d) and (e) give 0; the other cases hold as listed.
demonstrations.fails_without: With the counter missing, `test` would not give 5/5. Counting every landed retry regardless of change would give `fmt` 5. Whole-tree fingerprints only would give 0 for case (c).
demonstrations.seam: Production entry point: `gate_counts::gate_counts(&Records)` (pure). Guards: only request jobs with a Closed(Rejected) outcome and a verification, or Rejected/Failed with violations; retry link only through `reading::retried_job`; the retry must be Closed(Landed). Fixture: a `#[cfg(test)] pub(crate) mod fixtures` in gate_counts.rs (added in step 1) that builds the AnyRecords and loads them through `Records::load_dir` (exists, store.rs:353). No double holds the logic under test.

demonstrations.method: CLI integration tests in crates/athena-cli/tests/introspection.rs, plus Hestia, reading, proposals unit tests. A job chain is committed into the fixture repo: 5 jobs ended by `test`, each retried and landed unchanged (test overruled 5), and 2 jobs ended by `fmt` with no unchanged landing (overruled 0). The scripted `Model` answers with `prevention_kind: relax`, `gate: test`. `Athena::intervene` (category `mistake`) runs `introspect_intervention`, `introspect`, `apply_answer`, then `error_review`. Cases: relax accepted and queued; `remove` for `test` accepted; relax with `gate: null`, an unknown gate, or `fmt` (disagreements 0) gives a Failed record and queues nothing (finding 4); a second relax introspection for `test` in another job while the first gate request is open queues nothing, and after that request is closed queues one (finding 3). Hestia: `gate_review_*` (text has no bullet-like lines; second `error_review` queues nothing; `Athena::gate_review` called directly for a gate with disagreements 0 returns None; code-check A and relax B of one cause in two jobs: the backfill does not see the code-check cause as addressed by the gate request; `relax_introspection_is_in_no_repeated_cause_or_improvement`: two relax introspections of one class in two jobs give empty `repeated_causes` and no `improvement_of` item). Finding 1: proposals test `relax_and_remove_introspections_make_no_default_proposal` writes three jobs of relax cases and three of remove cases in one class through `read_records`; `generate` returns no proposal and no refusal, and a control of three Default cases still returns one. Finding 2: reading test `retry_seed_skips_relax_and_remove_introspections`: a job with a Recorded Rejection-trigger relax introspection (proposed_request, cause and prevention set) gives `retry_introspection` None and `has_retry_introspection` false; with an older code-check introspection also present the code-check one is returned; also for remove.
demonstrations.command: cargo test -p athena-cli --test introspection relax && cargo test -p athena-cli --test introspection remove && cargo test -p athena-core gate_review && cargo test -p athena-core relax_and_remove_introspections_make_no_default_proposal && cargo test -p athena-core retry_seed_skips_relax_and_remove_introspections && cargo test -p athena-core relax_introspection_is_in_no_repeated_cause_or_improvement
demonstrations.observes: The introspection is Recorded with `prevention_kind` Relax and a prevention starting `[gate: test] `. Exactly one new request job exists; its text has the line `Gate under review: test.`, the figures 'ended 5' and 'overruled 5', and the introspection id. A second `error_review`, or a second relax for the same gate while that request is open, queues nothing. `remove` is recorded. A null, unknown or zero-disagreement gate gives a Failed record and no request. No default proposal results from relax/remove cases; the retry seed ignores a relax record; no repeated cause or improvement item includes one.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the new kinds, `PreventionKind::parse` returns None and the record is Failed. Without the Hestia branch no request is queued (one introspection is not a repeated cause). Without the marker check, the second relax queues a second request. Without the disagreements >= 1 check, the `fmt` relax is queued citing 'overruled 0'. Without the read_records filter, three relax cases yield a default proposal. Without the retry_introspection filter, the seed holds 'relax: ...'. Without the cause_key exclusion, the backfill test finds the code-check cause addressed and queues nothing.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry points: `Athena::intervene`, reaching `Athena::introspect` (introspect.rs:1322) and `Athena::error_review` (hestia.rs:2347); `read_records` (introspect.rs:320) with `proposals::generate` (proposals.rs:265); `reading::retry_introspection` (reading.rs:1413); `hestia::repeated_causes` and `improvement_of`. Fakes: the existing scripted `Model` through `fx.athena(model.script(..))` (introspection.rs:36-73) and the real git fixture repo, both existing. Unit tests use existing helpers (`write_record`/`write_case` in proposals.rs tests, which gets a kind parameter in step 2b; `records_with` in reading.rs tests). The job-chain helper is added in step 9 in the test file; the test commits AnyRecords with `canonical_path()` and `to_json()` as review.rs `commit` does. Only the model's JSON reply is scripted; counting, validation, filtering and queuing run in production code.

demonstrations.method: The status test of criterion 4 asserts the order (most overruled first even though `fmt` sorts first by name; an ends-only key would tie or reverse). Then the diff is checked for governance files.
demonstrations.command: cargo test -p athena-cli --test introspection status_shows_gate && git diff --stat
demonstrations.observes: `athena status` lists the most overruled gate first. `git diff --stat` lists none of athena.toml, defaults.toml or .github/workflows.
demonstrations.fails_without: An unsorted list, a sort by name, or a sort by ends would fail the order assertion in the chosen fixture.
demonstrations.seam: Same as criterion 4: `athena status` through `Athena::status`, committed AnyRecords in the `Fixture` repo; the order assertion is in the same test.

open_questions: User: Should a later green rerun or the verifier passing the same change also count as a gate disagreement? The plan counts only the unchanged-landing signal, which is what criterion 1 requires. Adding the others later needs no record change.

User: Should the queued gate request name `athena.toml` in its Files line? The plan lists only `crates/` and `docs/`, because this job must not change governance files and the request is for Hestia's reviewer to decide.

User: Is it right that a gate request that has closed (landed, rejected or dropped) does not stop a new one for the same gate when a later relax answer arrives? The plan limits only one open request per gate, plus one per introspection id.
